beginner.headline: Today (Wed): workable-to-conditional morning before the weather turns. The south swell is fading but still has punch, a new long-period south pulse is starting to show, and a Flood Watch for Oʻahu starts this evening. Finish lessons by mid-afternoon.
beginner.recommendation: Plan on 9–11 AM on the rising tide while the wind is still light east. Watch Canoes from about 8:30 AM for several full set cycles, including the occasional long-period set, and check the post-set current before committing. Wrap up by about 3 PM; don't schedule late-afternoon lessons today.

tide.rule: High tide is not automatically the best lesson time. Combine tide with swell, current, wind and the student.

current.field_test: Watch how far you and the student are moved by one complete real set, and how much work it takes to get back in position.
current.one_student: Higher tolerance. You can shadow and manage drift.
current.multi_student: Lower tolerance: separation, more retrieval, less control. If current is strong, split the group, take one at a time, or reschedule.
